name: US-HealthBench
description: An open evaluation framework for LLM-based systems answering consumer-facing U.S. public-health questions (CDC, NIH, FDA, CMS) in English and Spanish: a pre-registered protocol, a five-dimension scoring rubric, an error taxonomy for consumer health AI, and a scoring implementation. Released alongside a post-freeze defect audit of the 2,020-item benchmark the framework produced, which passed 2,020/2,020 schema and source validation yet contains template collisions with contradicting gold answers (28.0% of items), encoding corruption (17.1% overall, 74.9% of Spanish items), splice contamination and source pollution. Re-scoring under two matching rules shows the resulting score distortion has no fixed direction: its sign is set by the scorer's matching rule rather than by the defect. The item set is released as provisional and is not fit for scoring systems; the transferable contribution is the defect taxonomy, the detection procedures, and the audit code.
